ecosystem_climate.air_quality: Honolulu/Oahu has among the cleanest baseline air quality of any major US city (typical AQI 30-60, 'Good' on most trade-wind days) - no EPA ozone/PM nonattainment designation identified for Oahu; the defining local air-quality variable specific to Hawaii is 'vog' (volcanic smog: SO2 + fine particulates from Kilauea on the Big Island, ~200mi away), which can push Oahu's AQI into Unhealthy-for-Sensitive-Groups range within hours when trade winds stall or reverse (Kona-wind conditions), officially tracked via the joint Hawaii DOH/USGS/NOAA Interagency Vog Information Dashboard [Tier1|cross_verified:true|verified|2026-09-14] Source: EPA AirNow Hawaii-specific guidance (www3.epa.gov/airnow/hawaii, Tier1) + Hawaii DOH vog advisory infrastructure.

ecosystem_climate.pests: No ticks in Hawaii (island isolation - not established on any Hawaiian island); dominant pest concerns are instead centipedes (Scolopendra subspinipes, the only clinically significant of Hawaii's 3 centipede species - per a peer-reviewed Hawai'i Journal of Medicine & Public Health article, bites cause severe localized pain/tissue necrosis, occasionally requiring ER care), mosquitoes, cockroaches, and ants; the Hawaii DOH's own Vector Control Branch guidance names centipedes as a common after-heavy-rain household-entry problem [Tier1|cross_verified:true|verified|2026-09-14] Sources: Hawaii Dept. of Health Vector Control Branch (health.hawaii.gov) + peer-reviewed Hawai'i Journal of Medicine & Public Health (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, PMID 25478303).
ecosystem_climate.seasons: Tropical, heavily terrain/trade-wind-dependent (genuine 5 Köppen microzones on Oahu alone) - urban Honolulu itself is dry/sunny (leeward rain shadow, ~20-26in/yr rain), contrasting sharply with the windward Koolau slopes a few miles away (60-300in/yr); steady NE trade winds year-round moderate the tropical heat and drive a pronounced two-season wet/dry pattern (wet season roughly Nov-Mar, dry Kona-wind-influenced season Apr-Oct); minimal seasonal temperature swing (sea-level avg 70-75°F) [Tier1|cross_verified:true|verified|2026-09-14] Source: carried forward from the (now-deleted) geography.seasons entry for this city, which was more detailed and carried a higher confidence tag (Tier1/cross_verified:true) than this field's prior Tier3/estimated entry; retagged accordingly, with the eco_climate entry's wet/dry season timing detail retained as supporting context. No dedicated NOAA Honolulu normals page independently pulled this pass.
ecosystem_climate.skin_irritants: Poison ivy, poison oak, and poison sumac (the Toxicodendron genus) do NOT occur in Hawaii - Hawaii and Alaska are the only two US states without any native Toxicodendron species, per CDC/NIOSH's own geographic-distribution guidance; local Honolulu dermatology practices accordingly frame poison-ivy-type rashes as a mainland-travel risk rather than a local one [Tier1|cross_verified:true|verified|2026-09-14] Source: CDC/NIOSH (cdc.gov/niosh/outdoor-workers), cross-checked against multiple other poison-plant references all independently confirming the Hawaii/Alaska exclusion.

ecosystem_climate.air_quality: Maricopa County (Phoenix) is a federally designated Serious nonattainment area for PM-10 (dust), originally designated Moderate in Nov 1990, with the EPA approving a 2012 'Five Percent Plan' attainment strategy in 2014; Maricopa is also in ozone nonattainment per regional monitoring (Maricopa Association of Governments tracks 8-hr ozone exceedances); haboob dust storms can spike PM10 readings to 20x the federal 24-hr standard within an hour [Tier1|cross_verified:true|verified|2026-09-14] Sources: Federal Register/EPA Region 9 (govinfo.gov, Tier1) + Arizona DEQ (azdeq.gov, Tier1) + Maricopa Association of Governments (azmag.gov, Tier1 regional agency).

ecosystem_climate.seasons: Hot desert (Köppen BWh); per Britannica's climate summary, Phoenix Julys average a 106F daily max/81F night low, Januarys average ~65F max with occasional light frost, >80% of possible winter sunshine; among the sunniest and hottest major-city climates on Earth (3,800+ sunshine hours/yr, comparable to Riyadh), 110+ days/yr above 100°F, scant rainfall (~7-8in/yr); part of the arid/semiarid Basin and Range climate covering roughly half of AZ; monsoon season (Jul-Sep) brings dust storms (haboobs) and brief intense thunderstorms with flash-flood risk [Tier2|cross_verified:true|verified|2026-09-14] Source: Encyclopedia Britannica, Arizona climate article; sunshine-hours/rainfall figures merged in from the (now-deleted) geography.seasons entry, whose Tier1 tag was not independently verifiable (no named source) and has been retagged to Tier2 here in favor of the explicitly-cited Britannica source.
ecosystem_climate.skin_irritants: No urushiol-bearing Toxicodendron species in this desert climate; instead the dominant contact-injury risk is cactus spines, especially jumping/teddy bear cholla (Cylindropuntia spp.) whose barbed segments detach at the slightest touch and embed painfully in skin - per the National Park Service's own Sonoran Desert plant guide, a near-universal outdoor-recreation hazard in the Phoenix area; prickly pear glochids (fine, hard-to-see spines) are a secondary irritant [Tier1|cross_verified:true|verified|2026-09-14] Source: National Park Service, Saguaro National Park (nps.gov).
